questions.q: Why does making your bed matter, according to McRaven?
a: A small early win builds pride and gives hope after a hard day
It proves to others that you are naturally disciplined
It is the only task that reliably predicts career success
It saves time later because you never have to tidy the room
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the small task creates a feeling of pride and a made bed makes tomorrow look better.

questions.q: What did ringing the bell during SEAL training mean?
a: You were quitting and would be released immediately
You had completed the day’s physical requirements
You were chosen to lead the next exercise
You had earned a rest break for the whole team
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that giving up was as easy as ringing the bell, which freed cadets on the spot.

questions.q: What did McRaven’s team learn from constantly finishing last in swimming?
a: The extra punishment made them stronger, and they won the final test
They needed to find a new coach before graduation
Swimming was the one skill they could never improve
Winning early mattered more than enduring hardship
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes how the Circus strengthened the team until they came first in the graduation test.

questions.q: What happened during Hell Week when the cadets sat covered in cold mud?
a: One man began to sing, and the others joined him
They were given warm blankets and sent back to camp
Several cadets rang the bell and ended their training
Their instructors ordered them to keep silent all night
questions.why: Lesson 3 recounts that one man started singing, others followed, and the mud felt less cold.

questions.q: What does McRaven’s rubber boat metaphor say about success?
a: You cannot paddle alone; you need good people with you
The strongest person should always steer the boat
A small boat is more reliable than a large one
Storms are the real test of any crew’s character
questions.why: Lesson 3 uses the boat to show that reaching your destination takes a team, not individual effort alone.
